plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole avenues turn lavender-blue as this graceful tree erupts in clouds of trumpet-shaped blossoms. The fallen flowers carpet pavements and lawns in violet. The fern-like leaves stay delicate and airy underneath.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring, roughly October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Pretoria, South Africa, and other Southern Hemisphere cities such as Sydney and Buenos Aires
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of the tens of thousands of these trees lining its streets. They were first planted there in the 1888.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: Dense, pom-pom-like and spidery blooms burst into color just as autumn leaves turn. They are a beloved fall garden plant, and they stay cheerful through the first cool nights and light frosts.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn, typically September to November in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Gardens across Japan, China, Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums have been cultivated in China for more than 2,000 years. Japan's Imperial family uses a stylized chrysanthemum as its crest.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Pale lilac, goblet-shaped flowers rise straight from bare ground in damp meadows, with no leaves in sight. They bring a surprising touch of spring-like delicacy to the autumn landscape.
plants.location: Meadows and woodland edges of western and central Europe
plants.funFact: The leaves appear months later, in spring, which gives it the nickname 'naked ladies'. All parts of the plant are highly toxic, and it is the source of the compound colchicine used in medicine.
